overall_summary: Space and cosmic extremes (exoplanets with bizarre rain, extreme temperatures, and sensory oddities) are the clear drivers of traffic and engagement for FACTVERSE, with videos like 'The Planet of Burning Ice' and 'TrES-2b' surpassing 1,000 views. Conversely, psychology and brain-related facts (e.g., fake memories, songs stuck in head) consistently underperform, rarely breaking 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Exoplanet & Cosmic Oddities with Sensory Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,055 views), 'TrES-2b: Darker Than Coal' (1,019 views), and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) are the top performers.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space phenomena, focusing on vivid, sensory-rich descriptions (burning ice, rubies, coal, smell of space).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees' (302 views) and 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (264 views) perform well above average.
winning_patterns.action: Create comparison-based hooks that challenge common sense or temporal understanding.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 53 views across multiple uploads) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Pause production on cognitive psychology and brain-trick content, as it lacks the immediate visual and curiosity appeal of cosmic extremes.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Space Facts Lacking Sensory/Visual Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' (11 views) and 'The Planet Where It Rains Liquid Metal!' (3 views) underperformed significantly.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely mathematical or abstract space facts; always ground space topics in extreme, easy-to-visualize environments.

next_video.concept: The Planet Made of Solid Diamond (55 Cancri e)
next_video.opening_direction: Start with a high-contrast visual of a sparkling planet and the hook: 'There is a planet in space made entirely of diamond, and it's twice the size of Earth.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the intense heat and pressure make it completely uninhabitable, with temperatures so high that the diamond surface is covered in flowing rivers of lava.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the highly successful 'extreme exoplanet' formula, combining high visual appeal (diamonds) with extreme cosmic conditions to drive high CTR and retention.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' cosmic scenario (e.g., 'What If a Black Hole Entered Our Solar System?') using the same high-contrast, sensory-rich visual style of the successful exoplanet videos to see if the audience interest translates to speculative space physics.
